title: The Man and His Two Sweethearts
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Man of middle age, whose hair was turning grey, had two Sweethearts, an old woman and a young one. The elder of the two didn't like having a lover who looked so much younger than herself; so, whenever he came to see her, she used to pull the dark hairs out of his head to make him look old.

The younger, on the other hand, didn't like him to look so much older than herself, and took every opportunity of pulling out the grey hairs, to make him look young. Between them, they left not a hair in his head, and he became perfectly bald.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many Sweethearts does the middle-aged Man have?
options: One
Three
Two
None; he was searching for one

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the elder Sweetheart dislike?
options: Having a lover who looked so much younger than herself
The Man's habit of visiting too rarely
The younger Sweetheart's jealousy
The color of the Man's clothing

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the elder Sweetheart do to the Man's hair?
options: She pulls out the grey hairs to make him look young
She dyes his hair a darker color
She trims his hair evenly all over
She pulls out the dark hairs to make him look old

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the younger Sweetheart dislike?
options: Having him look too young for her taste
Having him look so much older than herself
His habit of visiting the elder Sweetheart
His refusal to grow a beard

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the younger Sweetheart do to the Man's hair?
options: She pulls out the dark hairs to make him look old
She adds false hair to make him look younger
She pulls out the grey hairs to make him look young
She washes it carefully to keep it healthy

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the Man's hair in the end?
options: He becomes perfectly bald
He goes completely grey
He goes completely dark-haired again
He loses only a small amount of hair

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Man end up losing all his hair?
options: He decides to shave his head to please both women equally
He loses his hair naturally due to age, unrelated to either Sweetheart
One Sweetheart accidentally pulls out too much hair by mistake
Each Sweetheart pulls out the hairs she dislikes, and together they remove every hair he has

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Man's fate suggest about trying to please two people with opposite wishes?
options: It is always possible to satisfy two people if you are patient enough
Attempting to satisfy conflicting demands from both sides can leave you worse off than pleasing neither
Only one side's wishes ever truly matter in such a situation
The conflict between the two Sweethearts was ultimately harmless

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "elder" mean in "The elder of the two"?
options: The wealthier one
The taller one
The older one
The more talkative one

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Trying to satisfy two people with conflicting wants can end up leaving you with nothing at all
Grey hair is more attractive than dark hair to most people
Sweethearts should never disagree about appearance
Middle age is the best time to seek out new relationships

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what stage of life is the Man in?
options: Very old age, with hair already white
Young adulthood, with dark hair still full
Childhood, with no facial hair yet
Middle age, with hair turning grey

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when does the elder Sweetheart pull out the dark hairs?
options: Only once, the first time they met
Whenever he came to see her
Only on special occasions
Every morning before he woke up

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how often does the younger Sweetheart pull out the grey hairs?
options: Only once a year
Only when he asked her to
At every opportunity she got
Only when the elder Sweetheart was not present

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the two Sweethearts want opposite things from the Man's appearance?
options: Each wants him to appear closer to her own age
Each wants him to look as different as possible from the other woman
Each is trying to make him leave the other Sweetheart
Each is testing whether he truly loves her

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the outcome suggest about the Man's own role in the situation?
options: He actively pulled out his own hair to please them both
He was unaware that either woman was pulling out his hair
He asked both women to stop before losing all his hair
He appears to have gone along with both women rather than resisting either one

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "perfectly bald" mean in the passage?
options: Mostly grey with a few dark hairs left
Completely without any hair at all
Balding only in a small patch
Losing hair gradually over many years

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Man chooses one Sweetheart and ends the conflict peacefully
The two Sweethearts become friends and stop pulling his hair
Two Sweethearts each pull out hairs they dislike until the Man is left completely bald
The Man dyes his hair to satisfy both Sweethearts at once
